details.description: GPT-5.5 is OpenAI's general-purpose flagship model, released April 23, 2026 as the successor to GPT-5.4, with API access following on April 24. OpenAI positioned it as its most autonomous model yet for agentic coding, computer-use automation, knowledge work (documents, spreadsheets, analysis) and early-stage scientific research, with an adjustable reasoning effort (none through xhigh) and vision input. OpenAI's July 2026 GPT-5.6 family and, more recently, its September 2026 GPT-6 family (Astra, Sol, Luna) have since become OpenAI's current featured models; OpenAI's live API model documentation no longer lists GPT-5.5 among them, though the model remains reachable through the API.
advantages: Scores 93.6% on GPQA Diamond and 85.0% on ARC-AGI-2 (Verified), per OpenAI's launch benchmarks.
Reaches 82.7% on Terminal-Bench 2.0 and 58.6% on SWE-Bench Pro for agentic, command-line coding tasks, per OpenAI's launch benchmarks.
Scores 78.7% on OSWorld-Verified for computer-use tasks and 81.8% on CyberGym, per OpenAI's launch benchmarks.
Supports adjustable reasoning effort from none through xhigh plus vision (image) input, letting a caller trade latency for reasoning depth.
OpenAI reports it matches GPT-5.4's per-token serving latency while using fewer tokens to reach a given task's answer.
disadvantages: Superseded within OpenAI's own lineup first by the GPT-5.6 family (July 2026) and then by the GPT-6 family (Astra, Sol, Luna) launched September 2026; OpenAI's current model documentation no longer features GPT-5.5.
Text output only; does not generate images or audio.
Knowledge cutoff of December 1, 2025, per OpenAI's model documentation.
use_cases: Agentic software engineering: debugging, multi-file refactors and long command-line workflows
Knowledge work: generating and analyzing documents, spreadsheets and reports
Computer-use automation across tools and applications
Early-stage scientific research support, e.g. data analysis and literature synthesis
Long-context tasks such as reasoning over large codebases or document sets

notes: openai.com/index pages block direct automated fetches (HTTP 403); content was retrieved through a read-only fetch proxy and cross-checked against a third-party summary (Vellum) that matched the same numbers, so it is treated as opened. Catalog's max_input_tokens (1,000,000 and 1,050,000 across snapshots) and max_output_tokens (128,000) were kept as-is and not restated as a single figure. Artificial Analysis separately labels this model 'deprecated' in favor of GPT-5.6 Sol; OpenAI's own docs do not use that word for GPT-5.5, so the description says 'superseded' rather than 'deprecated'. Dropped an unverified third-hand claim (via a blog) that OpenAI's evaluations found GPT-5.5 'slightly more misaligned' than GPT-5.4 -- could not confirm it on the system card page itself.
